relationship.statement: A pendulum's period increases with the square root of its length, while bob mass has no effect. At small angles, the release angle barely changes the period, though wide swings take slightly longer.
assumptions: Air resistance and friction at the pivot are ignored.
The rod is massless and rigid, with all mass at the bob.
Downward gravitational acceleration is fixed at 9.81 m/s^2.

quantities.label: Length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the pendulum bob attached to the end of the rod.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Initial angle measured from the downward vertical line.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time for the bob to complete one full back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of complete back-and-forth swings per second.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the bob at the bottom of its swing.

quantities.label: Current angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle from the downward vertical line.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var g = 9.81; var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var theta0 = inputs.angle0 * Math.PI / 180; var k = Math.sin(theta0 * 0.5); var a = 1; var b = Math.cos(theta0 * 0.5); var a1 = (a + b) * 0.5; var b1 = Math.sqrt(a * b); var c1 = (a - b) * 0.5; var a2 = (a1 + b1) * 0.5; var b2 = Math.sqrt(a1 * b1); var c2 = (a1 - b1) * 0.5; var a3 = (a2 + b2) * 0.5; var b3 = Math.sqrt(a2 * b2); var c3 = (a2 - b2) * 0.5; var a4 = (a3 + b3) * 0.5; var c4 = (a3 - b3) * 0.5; var w0 = Math.sqrt(g / L); var period = (2 * Math.PI) / (w0 * a4); var frequency = 1 / period; var max_speed = 2 * Math.sqrt(g * L) * k; var K = Math.PI / (2 * a4); var u = K - w0 * t; var phi = 16 * a4 * u; phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin((c4 / a4) * Math.sin(phi))); phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin((c3 / a3) * Math.sin(phi))); phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin((c2 / a2) * Math.sin(phi))); phi = 0.5 * (phi + Math.asin((c1 / a1) * Math.sin(phi))); var theta = 2 * Math.asin(k * Math.sin(phi)); var angle = theta * 180 / Math.PI; var bob_x = L * Math.sin(theta); var bob_y = -L * Math.cos(theta); var bob_size = 0.2 + 0.6 * (m - 0.5) / 4.5; var diff = Math.cos(theta) - Math.cos(theta0); var speed = diff > 0 ? Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * diff) : 0; var dir = Math.cos(phi) >= 0 ? -1 : 1; var v_signed = dir * speed; var v_scale = 0.22; var vel_tip_x = bob_x + v_scale * v_signed * Math.cos(theta); var vel_tip_y = bob_y + v_scale * v_signed * Math.sin(theta); return { period: period, frequency: frequency, max_speed: max_speed, angle: angle, bob_x: bob_x, bob_y: bob_y, bob_size: bob_size, vel_tip_x: vel_tip_x, vel_tip_y: vel_tip_y, is_wide_swing: inputs.angle0 >= 40, is_short_rod: L <= 0.75, is_long_rod: L >= 1.5 }; }

Short rod gives a fast swing.
Long rod gives a slow swing.

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum's Swing?
lesson.description: Adjust the rod length, bob mass, and release angle of a swinging pendulum. Watch the motion and angle graph to discover which properties change the swing's timing and speed.
lesson.instructions: Drag the Length, Bob mass, and Release angle sliders to test each variable one at a time. Compare the live period, frequency, and peak speed readouts with the angle-versus-time plot, and pause or scrub time to inspect the swing.
lesson.goal: A pendulum's period grows with the square root of its length and slightly with wide angles, while bob mass leaves the timing unchanged.
